newsitem.title: USA: Intl Murex CEO comfortable with estimates.
newsitem.headline: Intl Murex CEO comfortable with estimates.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Toronto-based International Murex Technologies Corp said on Friday he is comfortable with analysts' consensus earnings estimates of $0.44 per share for this year and $0.10 a share for last year.

"We're comfortable with that," Chief Executive Robert Cusick said in an interview when asked about analysts' earnings estimates for the company this year after he spoke to the Atlanta chapter of the Stockbrokers Society.
He repeated that answer when asked about the estimates for 1996. He said 1996 earnings will be announced before March 1.
Murex is a medical diagnostic company whose best known product is its test to detect the Human Immunodeficiency Virus which is known to cause AIDS.
The return to profitability in 1996 compares to a net loss of $0.40 per share in 1995.
A major contributor to the turnaround was a settlement of a lawsuit filed against the company by Chiron Corp of Emeryville, California, which alleged that Murex had infringed on a Chiron patent.

Details of last August's settlement were not disclosed but the company reported that it took a $3.1 million charge against second quarter earnings for litigation settlements with Chiron and other parties that had also sued the company.
"Basically we were spending $5-$6 million a year on Chiron litigation, " Cusick told the Stockbrokers meeting. Chiron filed suit in 1992.
